newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analysts revise down eastern France maize yields.
newsitem.headline: Analysts revise down eastern France maize yields.

text.p: Maize combining is 75 percent complete in France's east, and local crop analysts say they have cut yield estimates after low temperatures slowed plant development in September and early October.
Analysts now target a regional yield of 9.2 tonnes per hectare, down from the 9.5 tonnes forecast last month.
But this would still represent a sharp rise from the 8.9 tonnes achieved in 1995.
Maize area is expected to increase to 126,000 hectares from 115,000.
"Yields levels remain decent but we are disappointed," one analyst for the local ONIC office in Strasbourg told Reuters.
The region is the country's third maize producer after the Aquitaine and Midi-Pyrenees regions in the southwest
The first cuts started in late September but farmers stopped combining when they realised the grain had not fully matured.
The harvest resumed in late October and may be over by November 20, analysts said.
One main concern has been high moisture levels found in the grain that was slow to mature.
Moisture levels reached 38 percent when the harvest started but recent cuts showed levels had come down to 35 percent.
Because the grain needed more time to dry out, its quality might be affected in the process, analysts warned.
Harvesting delays also created backlogs in some silos as farmers had been speeding up combining in recent days.
"Farmers have made an all-out effort to harvest their grain over the past days and this has led to tight spots in a few silos, but nothing to worry about," one analyst said.
